Article Text:
Riddhi Thakkar (in picture) was a resident of Kandivali West in Mumbai. She was travelling with a group of around 20 bikers from Raipur towards Kanker in Bastar region.

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think riding in groups increases the risk of motorcycle accidents? Yes, it can distract riders No, it promotes safety 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





RAIPUR: Riddhi Thakkar, a 24-year-old biker from Mumbai died after her motorcycle collided with a trailer truck on National Highway-30 near Markatola Ghat in Chhattisgarh’s Dhamtari district on Wednesday morning.Riddhi Thakkar was a resident of Kandivali West in Mumbai. She was travelling with a group of around 20 bikers from Raipur towards Kanker in Bastar region.The accident took place around 6am near Markatola, after her motorcycle collided with a trailer truck coming from the opposite direction. The impact left the motorcycle badly damaged and Riddhi seriously injured.Fellow bikers immediately took her to a private hospital in Dhamtari, where doctors treated her for severe injuries. However, she died during treatment.Police reached the hospital, completed the necessary formalities and sent Riddhi’s body for post-mortem. Her family was informed about the incident.The accident left members of the biking group in shock. Police are questioning fellow riders to establish the circumstances leading to the collision and are conducting further investigation.
Article Summary: Riddhi Thakkar, a 24-year-old biker from Mumbai died after her motorcycle collided with a trailer truck on National Highway-30 in Chhattisgarh’s Dhamtari district. She was travelling with a group of around 20 bikers from Raipur towards Kanker in Bastar region.

Article Title: What are Chud the Builder’s house arrest conditions? Charges, bond and release explained
Article Text:
What are Chud the Builder’s house arrest conditions? Charges, bond and release explained

Chud the Builder release and house arrest conditions

Chud the Builder charges and Tennessee cases

Dalton Eatherly, known online as “Chud the Builder,” is out of jail after posting bond in two Tennessee cases. The 28-year-old streamer had spent nearly three months in Montgomery County custody. Clarksville Now reported that he was released August 10, while WSMV confirmed he also posted a $15,000 bond in Davidson County. His release comes with strict rules, including house arrest, GPS monitoring, a gun ban and limits on travel.Chud the builder’s freedom is limited while both cases move forward. According to Clarksville Now, the Davidson County court ordered house arrest, a GPS ankle monitor, no access to weapons or firearms, and no entry into Davidson County unless he has a scheduled court appearance.His passport application must also be stopped or surrendered. The Montgomery County case has similar restrictions. Judge William Goodman III kept Eatherly’s $1 million bond in place and added a 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. curfew earlier in the case.The court also required GPS monitoring, the surrender of firearms and a gag order. Clarksville Now reported that the case has already been sent to a grand jury.WSMV reported that Eatherly posted the $1 million Montgomery County bond and then made the separate $15,000 Davidson County bond.The Nashville prosecutor’s office told the station it could seek to revoke his release if he commits another offense while awaiting trial.That means his release does not close either case, and he remains under court supervision while prosecutors continue the legal process. The conditions remain in place while both cases move through court.The more serious case comes from a May 13 shooting outside the Montgomery County Courts Center in Clarksville. Chud the Builder faces charges of attempted murder, employing a firearm during a dangerous felony, aggravated assault and reckless endangerment with a deadly weapon. Another man, Joshua Fox, was shot during the confrontation, and Eatherly was also injured.Court records and Clarksville Now reports say the case was sent to a grand jury. Details about what led to the shooting remain disputed, including Eatherly’s claim that he acted in self-defense. Since the case is still pending, the charges are allegations and have not been proven in court.Chud the Builder is also facing a separate Davidson County case tied to a May 9 incident at a Nashville restaurant. He was charged with theft of services of $1,000 or less, disorderly conduct and resisting arrest. WSMV reported that the case followed a dispute over a restaurant bill of about $400 after Eatherly was asked to stop livestreaming and leave.The two cases also come with separate limits on what Chud the Builder can say publicly. Clarksville Now reported that the Montgomery County order blocks discussion of the case through interviews and social media, while the Davidson County order also restricts public discussion of facts, evidence and witnesses. The restrictions do not decide whether Chud the Builder is guilty or innocent; that will be handled through the court process.
Article Summary: Dalton Eatherly, known online as “Chud the Builder,’ is out of jail after posting bond in two Tennessee cases. The 28-year-old streamer had spent nearly three months in Montgomery County custody. His release comes with strict rules, including house arrest, GPS monitoring, a gun ban and limits on travel.

Article Title: Who is Shaun Chen? Canadian MP of Indian-Chinese descent to resign this week, citing health reasons
Article Text:
Canadian MP ​Shaun Chen

Who is Shaun Chen?

His political career

PM Mark Carney thanks Chen

Liberal MP Shaun Chen has announced he will resign from the Canadian House of Commons this week, citing health problems linked to a serious car accident that have made it difficult for him to continue travelling to Ottawa.Chen, 45, has represented Scarborough North since 2015 and said he will step down on 15 August after more than a decade in federal politics.In a statement posted on X, Chen said he suffered significant health problems after a motor vehicle accident while travelling to Ottawa in late 2025.“After discussing the situation with my family, I have decided that it is best for me to step down as a Member of Parliament.”He described his time in Parliament as the “greatest privilege and honour” of his career and said he hoped his successor would enjoy representing the riding as much as he did.Chen was born in Toronto to Hakka Chinese parents from India and grew up in Scarborough, reflecting his Indian-Chinese heritage.Before entering federal politics, he spent years working in public education governance. He was first elected as a Toronto District School Board trustee in 2006, representing Scarborough-Rouge River.He later became vice-chair of the board and, in December 2014, was elected chair of the Toronto District School Board.He was the first Chinese-Canadian and the youngest person to lead Canada's largest school board.Chen left the position in 2015 to run for Parliament.Chen was elected as the Liberal MP for Scarborough North in October 2015 and was re-elected in 2019, 2021 and 2025.During his time in Parliament, he served on committees covering areas including citizenship and immigration, Canadian heritage, public accounts, science and research, veterans affairs and the status of women.His political work has included issues affecting children and young people, education, immigration, seniors and public services.Chen said his decision to resign was made after discussions with his family as his health continued to affect his ability to travel to Ottawa.Prime Minister Mark Carney thanked Chen for his years of public service and highlighted his work with young people and efforts to combat racism.“Wishing you a full recovery and best of luck for what comes next. I know you'll keep making a difference for years to come,” Carney said.Chen's departure adds to a growing number of Canadian MPs leaving Parliament this year.Several federal byelections are already scheduled for 31 August, while further vacancies are expected to be filled through future by-elections.
Article Summary: Liberal MP Shaun Chen has announced he will resign from the Canadian House of Commons this week. Chen, 45, has represented Scarborough North since 2015 and said he will step down on 15 August after more than a decade in federal politics. He said he suffered significant health problems after a motor vehicle accident while travelling to Ottawa in late 2025.

Article Title: F-16 fighter jet crashes in Turkey during training flight, pilot safe
Article Text: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova on Wednesday, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft.In a statement posted on social media, the ministry said the aircraft went down during a routine training mission and that the pilot safely bailed out before the crash.The exact cause of the accident will be determined following a detailed investigation, the ministry added.A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site following the incident, local media reported.Live footage broadcast by Turkish news channel NTV showed a fireball and thick black smoke rising from the wreckage, visible from several locations across the province.
Article Summary: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova. According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft. A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site.

Article Title: Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp, Walt Nauta: 3 aides were allowed with Trump when he was moved into a catering truck during Turkey emergency
Article Text:
Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp and Walt Nauta are the closest aides allowed inside the catering truck that hid President Donald Trump in Turkey.

Who is Dan Scavino?

Who is Natalie Harp?

Who is Walt Nauta?

No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Apart from some low-ranking aides, only three individuals were allowed inside the truck, as they are believed to be the closest to the president: Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations. Washington Post reported that neither Marco Rubio nor Pete Hegseth nor Stephen Miller were allowed inside the truck that took TrumpThe catering truck moved under concealment from the Air Force One aircraft to a smaller Air Force C-32A before flying to Britain separately.Dan Scavino has been serving as the White House deputy chief of staff in the second Trump administration but his history with Trump dates back to 1992, when he worked as a caddie at a New York country club that Trump later purchased and turned into Trump National Golf Club Westchester. After graduating from college, Scavino worked his way up to become the golf club's general manager.He joined Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and went on to serve throughout the entire first Trump administration as White House Director of Social Media and later Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications.During that time, he was particularly known for managing Trump's personal social media presence and online strategy. He remained a central advisor at Mar-a-Lago following the 2020 election, worked as a senior official on the 2024 campaign, and returned to senior White House leadership upon Trump taking office again in 2025.Natalie Harp is an American political aide and former television presenter who serves as Executive Assistant to the President in Donald Trump's second White House administration. She is the one who handles the president's daily schedule and is always spotted with him. Known colloquially among campaign staffers and media outlets as Trump's "human printer," Harp earned a reputation for constantly accompanying him with a portable printer to feed him printed news articles, polls, and favorable commentary. In her role as executive assistant, she remains a member of his inner circle, assisting with his daily schedule and managing dictation for his social media accounts.Walt Nauta is a close political aide to Donald Trump and currently serves in his second White House administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Director of Oval Office Operations. Nauta spent 20 years in the U.S. Navy, reaching the rank of Senior Chief Petty Officer. During his military career, he was assigned to the Presidential Food Service and eventually became a White House valet during Trump's first presidency. In that role, he acted as a personal assistant and "body man," handling day-to-day tasks like fetching beverages and managing travel details.After Trump left office in 2021, Nauta retired from the Navy and joined Trump's personal staff at Mar-a-Lago, continuing to work as his primary executive assistant and political aide. He later drew widespread national attention when he was indicted alongside Trump in June 2023 in the federal classified documents case, where prosecutors accused him of helping move and conceal boxes of sensitive materials.
Article Summary: No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations, are believed to be the closest aides to the president.

Article Title: Thailand visit, Suu Kyi access: Can Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing win political legitimacy?
Article Text:
Min Aung Hlaing in Thailand; Aung San Suu Kyi with ICRC official

Min Aung Hlaing's ascent to power

Significance of Aung San Suu Kyi

Why Thailand visit matters for Min Aung Hlaing - and how Bangkok differs from ASEAN

Can regional engagement help Min Aung Hlaing’s legitimacy push?

Min Aung Hlaing’s continuing legitimacy challenge

Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week, in a trip that carried significance beyond routine diplomacy. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency.That visit to Thailand coincided with another significant development in Myanmar. Aung San Suu Kyi , the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor. On August 3, Suu Kyi met Arnaud de Baecque, the International Committee of the Red Cross' (ICRC) resident representative in her country.Naypyidaw also released photographs of the meeting—the first official images of the former State Counsellor in years.Was the close timing of the two developments just a coincidence? For Min Aung Hlaing, who came to power by overthrowing an elected government rather than through the ballot box, both developments could be part of a broader effort to build political legitimacy and gain wider international acceptance.During his visit to Thailand, the 70-year-old former military leader sought to reassure his host, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, that Myanmar was “returning to democracy.”"Myanmar has now re-established itself on the path to democracy and is moving toward a better future," Min Aung Hlaing told Charnvirakul.The remarks stood in sharp contrast to the circumstances of his rise to the presidency. His claim that Myanmar is on a “democratic path” also comes against the backdrop of a bloody civil war triggered by the coup that brought him to power.According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent organisation that documents arrests and casualties linked to the Myanmar civil war, more than 8,200 civilians had been killed and 31,645 people arrested by the regime's security forces as of August 5.Besides, the parliamentary elections under Min Aung Hlaing in late 2025 and early 2026 were also widely criticised as “neither free nor fair” as the army-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party swept the elections, winning 232 of the 263 contested seats in the lower house and 109 of 157 seats in the upper house. Ahead of the presidential election in April—Myanmar's first since 2018—he resigned from the military and was subsequently elected president.However, his transition to the presidency did little to ease international scepticism. Major democracies withheld congratulations following his victory.For Myanmar, Aung San Suu Kyi’s significance extends beyond her role as the head of the country’s first democratically elected civilian government in 50 years and the military’s toppling of her administration.For many inside and outside Myanmar, the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize laureate remains the country's most recognisable symbol of democratic rule and civilian legitimacy.In 2022, Suu Kyi was sentenced to 33 years in prison on a series of charges that her supporters and rights groups described as “politically motivated” and intended to prevent her return to politics. Later, her sentence was reduced to 27 years and, in April, to 18 years, while she was transferred to house arrest.Against this backdrop, the meeting with the ICRC representative was significant because it marked the first confirmed contact between Suu Kyi, 81, and an independent international organisation since her house arrest. It was also her first confirmed communication with the outside world since she wrote a letter to her son from prison in early 2024.Sreeparna Banerjee, an Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF), agreed that both developments could be seen as part of Myanmar’s broader effort to “manage its international image,” but said it cannot be assumed that the moves were directly linked.“The timing is noteworthy, but it would be difficult to establish a direct connection between the two developments at this stage… Access to Aung San Suu Kyi after a prolonged period of isolation could signal some limited openness, while Min Aung Hlaing’s high-profile visit to Thailand demonstrates Myanmar’s attempt to expand diplomatic engagement,” Banerjee, whose work focuses on Myanmar and Thailand, told The Times of India.For Min Aung Hlaing, the bigger challenge remains turning such diplomatic engagement into wider political legitimacy and international acceptance.According to Banerjee, the visit was important for Min Aung Hlaing because it offered him a degree of political normalisation.“Being received at the highest level by an ASEAN neighbour allows him to project the image of a leader whose government is once again engaging with the region rather than remaining diplomatically isolated,” she said.Significantly, while Thailand and Myanmar are both ASEAN member states, Bangkok’s approach towards Naypyidaw differs from that of the rest of the 11-nation bloc of Southeast Asian states.Thailand has continued to engage with Myanmar despite ASEAN barring Min Aung Hlaing from its top-level meetings over the non-implementation of the Five-Point Consensus agreed with the grouping after he seized power.On this, Banerjee observed that the real value of Bangkok’s “bridge” diplomacy — acting as a bridge between Myanmar and ASEAN — would depend on whether Thailand can use it to encourage some meaningful progress on the Five-Point Consensus.Additionally, ASEAN is yet to recognise the results of Myanmar’s 2025–26 parliamentary elections. The bloc has also repeatedly called for Suu Kyi’s unconditional release, renewing the demand after her meeting with the ICRC official. The regime rebuffed this call too.For its part, Thailand has described its approach vis-à-vis Myanmar as one of “calibrated re-engagement” aimed at keeping dialogue open while responding to “realities on the ground.” Bangkok has also argued that Myanmar is essential to ASEAN unity and regional stability, provided it remains peaceful and stable.In addition to being barred from top-level ASEAN summits, Min Aung Hlaing faces Western sanctions over his role in toppling Suu Kyi’s government, the subsequent civil war, and the alleged persecution of the Rohingya minority in the Rakhine province.The Thailand visit was his fourth overseas trip since becoming president, following visits to India, China, and Laos. India was the only democratic country among the four destinations, underscoring the limited engagement he has so far had with democratic governments.Despite this, and close ties with Russia, he has remained largely isolated internationally.So, can his engagement with Thailand and his wider regional outreach — help him in his bid for greater international recognition and acceptance?Sreeparna Banerjee, the ORF Associate Fellow, suggested that even regional acceptance remains uncertain at this stage, despite such engagement being an important part of Myanmar’s quest for political legitimacy.“Naypyidaw appears determined to engage on its own terms rather than fully follow the ASEAN framework. Thailand's outreach may create space for dialogue, but whether this translates into wider regional acceptance remains uncertain,” she explained.She also highlighted that uncertainty over Myanmar’s regional acceptance stems in part from the fact that Singapore will take over the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027. The city-state has repeatedly called for full implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.This underscores the scale of the challenge facing Min Aung Hlaing in his bid for wider acceptance.For a leader who rises to power as Min Aung Hlaing did, securing international recognition is likely to remain a gradual and difficult process.The regime’s refusal to release Suu Kyi, a global icon, further complicates that effort.Engagement with neighbouring countries can provide an important opening, but broader recognition often depends on how other governments assess the resulting political situation. Yet for Min Aung Hlaing, this remains the only option to secure recognition.For now, engagement with Thailand may offer Min Aung Hlaing some diplomatic space, but whether it can translate into legitimacy for him remains uncertain.
Article Summary: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency. Aung San Suu Kyi, the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor.

Article Title: Delhi Mosque Demolition: Delhi Demolition Drive Near Faiz-e-Elahi Mosque: Police Clash During MCD Action
Article Text:
Delhi demolition drive: MCD carries out action near Faiz-e-Elahi mosque following HC order; 5 cops injured in stone pelting

Delhi: 5 Cops Injured, 10 Detained As Anti-Encroachment Drive Near Mosque Turns Violent

Demolition drive at Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque near Turkman Gate in Delhi on Wednesday. Image Credit: Tarun Rawat/TNN







NEW DELHI: Multiple police personnel were injured during a demolition drive in central Delhi early on Wednesday after locals and miscreants attacked them with stones.The police is trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting and will initiate strict action against them.Delhi Police have registered an FIR against unknown persons and around 10 people have been detained for questioning so far, officials said.Police are scanning CCTV footage, ground visuals and body-camera recordings to identify those involved in the attack on the police team.While the FIR has been lodged against unidentified persons, investigators said four to five suspects have already been identified and further legal action will follow.Special commissioner (Law and Order) Ravindra Yadav said that the action started around 1 am."MCD conducted demolition as per the high court's orders on the encroached land. Stones were pelted at the police at night. We used minimal force to push back."DCP (Central) Nidhin Valsan said, "The action is still ongoing. We deployed our staff for security. 4 to 5 officers suffered minor injuries. As soon as we get the CCTV camera footage, ground footage, and body camera footage, we will identify the miscreants and take legal action."The demolition was carried out by the MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area. The drive kicked off around 1 am, with around 17 bulldozers pressed into service.The action followed an order of the Delhi High Court, which declared a dispensary and a community hall adjoining the mosque illegal and directed their removal.The administration appealed to local residents to maintain peace.Anticipating major disruptions, the Delhi Traffic Police also issued a traffic advisory, warning of congestion on several key roads on Wednesday. Traffic around Ramlila Maidan and adjoining areas is expected to remain affected through the day.
Article Summary: 5 cops injured in stone pelting during demolition drive in central Delhi. Police are trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting. The demolition was carried out by MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area.

Article Title: Laxmi Nagar assault: New clip shows SUV crashing into house; accused Omkar Yadav claims self-defence in viral video
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Another CCTV clip related to the Laxmi Nagar assault has surfaced, showing a group of men arriving first, opening a gate and assaulting a man. Moments later, a Thar SUV was seen speeding towards the house and crashing into the wall, after which several men got out of it and the assault continued. Meanwhile, accused Omkar Yadav has released a video on social media defending his brother, gym caretaker and key accused Satish Yadav alias Pintu Yadav.A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault recently when the man was beaten up, his wife was said to be molested, and their son was stripped and assaulted on the street.The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business, leading to the dispute. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage-related issue, Yadav, along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son, a senior officer said.An earlier CCTV footage had shown the couple's son being dragged onto the road, stripped and beaten up by a group of four-five men. The presence of police personnel in parts of the footage also raised questions. Police claimed the assault stopped after they arrived while the victims alleged that they were beaten up in full view of the cops, a claim that is being verified.According to the complaint, the couple's son came out after hearing the commotion and was assaulted. The couple also said their two sons had left the house following the attack.Police said main accused Yadav was arrested while the other accused were absconding. Omkar, one of the absconding accused, posted a video on social media, saying his brother had been working with the complainant for "20-25 years" and was running the gym for the past "12-13 years". He questioned why objections over the gym were raised only in the past five-six months. "If we captured the land, why did she start complaining only now?" he asked.Omkar further alleged that the legal proceedings were "one-sided" and claimed that he was also being targeted. He identified himself as a worker of a party and alleged that he was being defamed by an opposition party.Referring to the incident, Omkar said, "On Jan 2, I got a call from my brother. I reached the spot after 10-15 minutes. If I am seen kicking two or three times in the video, it was in self-defence. They started hitting first."A case has been registered at the Laxmi Nagar police station under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful restraint, criminal trespass, assault or use of criminal force to outrage the modesty of a woman, acts intended to insult a woman's modesty and criminal intimidation.
Article Summary: A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault. The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage- related issue, Yadav along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son.

Article Title: CJP leader vs Puducherry Police: Saurav Das alleges family harassment, cops say ‘routine’ security check
Article Text:
Saurav Das alleged police visited his family home for questioning





NEW DELHI: A political controversy erupted in Puducherry after Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das alleged that police visited his family’s residence and questioned his relatives, accusing the BJP-backed Puducherry government of intimidating his family at the “behest of the Union government”.Puducherry Police, however, said the visit was part of routine security checks ahead of Independence Day.In a post on X, Das questioned the reason for the police visit and asked whether such questioning was part of the legal procedure."Two hours ago, the Pondicherry Police showed up at my family's home and subjected them to all kinds of questioning. Why this harassment, @PuducheryPolice? Who ordered this and for what purpose? Is this the legal procedure?" Das wrote.He further alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party-backed (BJP) government in Puducherry was "intimidating" his family and claimed that the action was not in keeping with the character of the Union Territory government."Why is the BJP government in Pondicherry intimidating my family? This is not the character of the Pondy government. This is being done at the behest of the Union government!" he said.He alleged that the police visit was aimed at intimidating him into remaining silent and said he would not back down from his political activities."If the intention is to intimidate me into silence, it will not work. This will not cower me down. It only strengthens our resolve to build a better system, one where the police uphold the law instead of acting like goondas!" the post read.Das also questioned the basis of the police action, asking who had ordered it and why his family was being questioned.Das also referred to Union Home Minister Amit Shah's visit to Puducherry two days earlier, during which he met the Union Territory's Home Minister and Lieutenant Governor."Just two days ago, Amit Shah was in Puducherry, where he met its Home Minister and Lieutenant Governor (who was infamously known as the 'Eyes and Ears' of Modi in Gujarat years). Was this intimidation tactic planned at their meeting?" Das wrote.Puducherry Police, meanwhile, rejected the suggestion that the questioning was linked to political intimidation and said the visit was part of security arrangements ahead of Independence Day.Police said enquiries were being conducted at houses and hotels in areas frequented by VIPs to check whether any new persons had recently arrived or were staying in Puducherry.The police said such enquiries were routine and part of the security measures being undertaken ahead of August 15.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: CJP co-convenor Saurav Das alleged that police visited his family's residence and questioned his relatives. He accused the BJP-backed Puducherry government of intimidating his family at the “behest of the Union government’ PudUCherry Police, however, said the visit was part of routine security checks ahead of Independence Day.

Article Title: Booking for meet cancelled in Delhi due to political pressure: CJP
Article Text:
The Cockroach Janta Party alleged political pressure caused a banquet hall to cancel their meeting





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Wednesday alleged that a banquet hall in Naraina cancelled its booking for a meeting of volunteers due to alleged "political pressure", forcing the group to hold the meeting at a nearby park, where it faced disruption from locals."When we reached the venue Wednesday, the owner said they could not let us hold the meeting as there was pressure from local BJP and RSS functionaries... In the past few days, we have been denied bookings by at least 10 places, citing similar pressure," CJP spokesperson Saurav Das told TOI.Das alleged four-five people tried to disrupt the park meeting. "Some of them had earlier tried to create a ruckus outside (CJP founder) Abhijeet Dipke's house. Police did not remove the locals," he alleged.Videos on social media showed heated exchanges between locals and CJP volunteers.Delhi BJP spokesperson Praveen Shankar Kapoor said BJP govt had allowed CJP to protest at Jantar Mantar and, therefore, there was no reason for the party to pressure a private banquet hall to deny permission.A police officer said locals showed concern over the meeting being held at the park, but police ensured the situation remained peaceful. TOI didn't get any response from the banquet.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) alleged a banquet hall in Naraina cancelled its booking for a meeting of volunteers due to alleged "political pressure" The group had to hold the meeting at a nearby park, where it faced disruption from locals. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das alleged four-five people tried to disrupt the park meeting.

Article Title: Maharashtra assembly Speaker wants Shivaji Maharaj slogans on trains arriving at and departing from CSMT in Mumbai
Article Text:
Rahul Narwekar has urged Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw to include the slogans ‘Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Ki Jai’ and 'Jai Bhavani, Jai Shivaji’ in announcements made on every train arriving at or departing from CSMT

Mumbai:





Maharashtra Legislative Assembly Speaker Rahul Narwekar has urged Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw to include the slogans, ' Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Ki Jai’ and 'Jai Bhavani, Jai Shivaji’, in announcements made on every train arriving at or departing from Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT).Narwekar submitted a letter to Vaishnaw during his visit to Delhi, seeking the inclusion of the slogans along with routine railway announcements at CSMT.In his letter, Narwekar said CSMT is not merely a historic railway station, but also a symbol of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s ideals of courage, Swarajya and patriotism. Thousands of passengers from across the country travel through the station every day, making it an important platform to spread awareness about the legacy and ideals of Shivaji Maharaj, he said.Narwekar said the proposed announcements would help introduce younger generations to Shivaji Maharaj’s administration, bravery, welfare-oriented policies and commitment to national interest. He also highlighted Shivaji Maharaj’s role in bringing together people from different sections of society while establishing Swarajya.Narwekar requested Vaishnaw to consider the proposal positively and issue necessary directions to the railway administration to incorporate the two slogans in announcements on all trains arriving at and departing from CSMT.Narwekar expressed confidence that the initiative would help carry the message of Shivaji Maharaj’s contribution and the ideals of Swarajya beyond Maharashtra through the extensive railway network.
Article Summary: Rahul Narwekar has urged Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw to include the slogans in announcements made on every train arriving at or departing from CSMT.Narwekar said CSMT is not merely a historic railway station, but also a symbol of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s ideals of courage, Swarajya and patriotism.

Article Title: Vile Parle fire: Building’s safety system kept in manual mode, only 2 knew how to operate it
Article Text:
The fire broke out in a flat in which the developer and the family lived on the 11th floor of Shanta Bhuvan in Vile Parle

Mumbai:





The 12-storey Vile Parle building where a 23-year-old domestic help and a developer’s two-year-old grandson died in a fire in a flat late on Tuesday did not have a fully automated firefighting system and only two people knew how to operate it, shows an initial probe.Fire brigade officials said the sprinklers installed outside the 11th floor flat of Shanta Bhuvan where the fire broke out failed to get activated. “The firefighting system could not generate enough power on its own and was kept in manual mode. Had the sprinklers turned on, they could have helped control the spread of the fire. The security guards, too, did not know how to operate the system,” said an official. BMC additional commissioner Vipin Sharma said only two members of the family of developer Hiren Batavia, who constructed the building and lived in the affected flat, knew how to operate the system. It wasn’t clear who these two members were.The building received its occupancy certificate in 2020.The help, Ankita Chhetri (23), and the toddler, Abir Siddharth Batavia, were found unconscious in one of the bathrooms attached to a bedroom and later declared dead. “Once the fire flared up, Chhetri moved to one of the bedrooms, where the toddler was. When the fire intensified, she took the toddler in her arms and moved to the bathroom,” said an official.Officials believe that both could have survived had Chhetri opened the sliding windows of the bedroom. Six others, including a fire personnel, sustained injuries. Around 15 occupants were rescued from the building.Hiren (64) managed to escape with his granddaughter as the fire began to spread. He raised an alarm while getting out and alerted occupants of nearby flats. The fire later spread to an adjacent flat. Abir’s parents were out on a stroll when the tragedy occurred.Parth Batavia (32), another son of Hiren, was in the bathroom of another bedroom. He failed to hear his father’s screams and realised there was a fire only after he came out of the bathroom, said a fire official. “He placed himself almost outside the large sliding glass window and near the safety grille and was able to get fresh air. Besides, he also tied a handkerchief over his face. He kept speaking to his relatives on the phone during the period. Subsequently, fire brigade personnel rescued him.”The fire brigade is yet to confirm the cause of the fire, but the family claimed that Chhetri left a hot iron unattended on a table in the hall. Officials said the fire could have originated elsewhere, possibly in an AC unit.After finding Chhetri and Abir, fire brigade personnel, led by station officers A S Khanolkar and RS Pawade, performed CPR on them. “We administered CPR continuously for about 15 minutes till they were shifted to the hospital,” said an official.
Article Summary: Fire brigade officials said the sprinklers installed outside the 11th floor flat of Shanta Bhuvan where the fire broke out failed to get activated. The help, Ankita Chhetri (23), and the toddler, Abir Siddharth Batavia, were found unconscious in one of the bathrooms attached to a bedroom and later declared dead.

Article Title: Doctor at Kalyan’s Civic Hospital Served Notice Over False Dog Bite Info
Article Text:
Representative Picture

Thane:





The medical officer at the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation’s Rukminibai Hospital has been served a show-cause notice for allegedly providing incorrect information regarding dog bite cases on Sunday, civic officials informed on Wednesday.The facility actually attended to 58 dog bite patients on Sunday, but Dr. Sandeep Pagare, medical officer at the facility, apparently failed to verify it and claimed 130 people were bitten. As a result, the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation came under criticism from residents and activists who raised questions over the apparent apathy of the administration.The notice served by Chief Medical Officer Dr Deepa Shukla has asked the MO to respond within 24 hours, and in case he fails to reply, the administration would assume he has nothing to say and would proceed with appropriate disciplinary action.“The doctor possibly failed to get the correct information and released the information without confirming the actual position that caused visible panic among residents. The notice is likely to serve as a warning to other staff not to casually share sensitive information without confirming facts,” said a senior doctor refusing to be identified.
Article Summary: The medical officer at the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation’s Rukminibai Hospital has been served a show-cause notice for allegedly providing incorrect information regarding dog bite cases. The notice served by Chief Medical Officer Dr Deepa Shukla has asked the MO to respond within 24 hours, and in case he fails to reply, the administration would proceed with appropriate disciplinary action.

Article Title: Vile Parle building fire: Domestic help likely tried to save toddler, both choked to death
Article Text:
The fire broke out in a flat in which the developer and the family lived on the 11th floor of Shanta Bhuvan in Vile Parle

Mumbai:





Even in her final moments, little Abir was on Ankita Chhetri’s mind. Officials believe the Batavia family’s domestic help grabbed him from one of the bedrooms as the fire spread and took shelter in the attached bathroom. Rescuers found Abir lying on her chest, both unconscious. CPR on them failed.They were declared dead at Nanavati Hospital. At Cooper Hospital’s postmortem examination centre, officials said they died of asphyxiation and did not sustain burn injuries.Four other members of the Batavia household were taken to Nanavati Hospital, including the developer, Hiren Batavia. They were discharged after being kept under observation through the night. Two others, a fireman and the watchman, were taken to Cooper Hospital for minor injuries. They were discharged as well after treatment.Abir’s parents, Siddharth Batavia and Jayni Batavia, arrived with the extended family to claim his remains on Wednesday. The wait was long due to a few others in the queue. “We are very distraught, we have no option but to wait,” said one of the extended family members. The family could only take possession of the body by around 1pm.A case of accidental death was registered at Santacruz police station.Senior inspector Dattatray Masavekar said Chhetri was a native of West Bengal and her family has been contacted. “We are still finding out more details about her,” he said. Until her family arrives in the city, her postmortem remains pending due to lack of consent from blood relatives. Some of her distant relatives had tried to claim the body earlier in the day; they could not be traced till the time of going to press.
Article Summary: The fire broke out in a flat in which the developer and the family lived on the 11th floor of Shanta Bhuvan in Vile Parle. Officials believe the Batavia family’s domestic help grabbed him from one of the bedrooms as the fire spread and took shelter in the attached bathroom.

Article Title: 1,100-page chargesheet filed in Mumbai train murder case; Govt Railway Police seeks special prosecutor
Article Text:
21-year-old Mayank Lohar was killed by a co-traveller on a local train over a trivial dispute on keeping the compartment door shut. His family has demanded strictest punishment possible for the perpetrator

Mumbai:





The Govt Railway Police (GRP) on Wednesday submitted a 1,100-page-long chargesheet before a magistrate court in the murder of a 21-year-old commuter, Mayank Lohar, by a co-traveller, Roshan Suvarna, over an argument about keeping a train compartment door open amid heavy rain.GRP has requested that the case be fast-tracked and a special public prosecutor be appointed, given the heinous nature of the crime.The chargesheet contains statements of 68 witnesses. Among these are six to seven prime witnesses who were present in the first-class compartment of the Nalasopara-bound fast local train on June 23 when Suvarna stabbed Lohar. Eyewitnesses recounted that Suvarna was visibly drunk. He wanted to keep the door of the compartment open, but rainwater was entering inside and Lohar shut it. There was a heated exchange of words between the two and Suvarna landed the first blow on Lohar, who retaliated in defence. Shortly, a few other passengers sent away Suvarna to another exit. Subsequently, he took a large knife from his bag and went over to Lohar, stabbing him in his chest and abdomen.One of the passengers filmed the moment, also capturing the blood-soaked compartment.The video clip forms crucial evidence in the case. Suvarna hopped off the train at Borivli station and threw away the knife. He was arrested from Panvel while he was trying to leave the city the next day. The chargesheet contains the statement of a restaurant manager whose colleagues found the 17.5-cm-long knife dumped in a lane outside Borivli (W) station. Forensic analysis confirmed the knife found in the lane was the one used in the murder. Police have also recorded the statement of a friend of Suvarna’s who works with an e-commerce platform and from whom Suvarna had picked up two knives. He kept the small knife at this workplace for making barcode labels and carried the large knife in his bag for seven months until the crime.
Article Summary: Mayank Lohar, 21, was killed by a co-traveller on a local train over a trivial dispute on keeping the compartment door shut. His family has demanded strictest punishment possible for the perpetrator Roshan Suvarna. Govt Railway Police (GRP) on Wednesday submitted a 1,100-page-long chargesheet before a magistrate court.
